clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's house every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton's drinking rose and he and his wife separated; your mother's anxiety over Anton rose; your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter; and your grandmother took a job at the library and her functioning came back by May 1979. The shifts pile up from February through May, each one near another's, and settle as Delphine's life steadied. clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis with Parkinson's disease in September 1986, within the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father's anxiety rose as he phoned his father nightly for news; he and your uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather had chest pains; Hazel's functioning fell again after a brief rise; your father took her to the clinic twice a week and your great-aunt Mavis came to nurse her; your father drank most evenings; your aunt Pearl's anxiety rose; and by February 1996 your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side. The shifts run unevenly across a decade, each step a fall or a tightening with only partial relief between them, so the period holds as one climb. By June 1997 Hazel moved to the nursing home and the tight overfunctioning settled.
